newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon shares firm, boosted by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon shares firm, boosted by blue chips.

text.p: Singapore shares trekked higher at noon on Friday helped by demand for blue chips but with small capitalisation issues continuing to hog the limelight.
Dealers said the market was rebounding after recent falls and partly also on a firmer mood inspired by Wall Street gains.
"It's firmer on the back of the Dow Jones, but activity is still mainly on recent new share issues," a remisier said.

About half of market volume was being driven by small issues like equipment company Poh Lian at Singapore $0.54, up two cents and Tye Soon, which hit a high of S$0.585 and held at noon around S$0.57, up one cent.
Institutional demand for blue chips, however, also lifted the soggy Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) after recent falls.
The STII rose 19.68 points to 1,982.08. Overall turnover was 82 million shares with gainers outpacing loser 196 to 79.
Dealers said despite the brief blip, the market was not likely to hold onto gains as fundamentals remained poor.
"Hong Kong may be off at the moment, but they should perform relatively well compared to the region," a foreign brokerage dealer said, noting Singapore and Malaysia had been downgraded.
Among gainers were Singapore Press Holdings foreign at S$29.60, and Fraser & Neave at S$10.20, up 30 cents.
